Let
\[
M_n=\frac{1}{2\cos\frac{\pi}{2n}}.
\]
The largest possible value is
\[
\boxed{|\alpha|=M_n}.
\]

When equality is attained,
\[
\boxed{\beta=\frac{(-1)^n}{2n}\tan\frac{\pi}{2n}\left(\frac{\alpha}{|\alpha|}\right)^n}
\]
with \(\alpha\ne0\).

Proof sketch, self-contained:

Rotate \(\theta\) so that \(\alpha=a\ge0\) is real. Averaging \(P(\theta)\) and \(P(-\theta)\) lets us assume \(\beta=b\in\mathbb R\) without changing \(a\). Then
\[
P(\theta)=1+2a\cos\theta+2b\cos n\theta.
\]

Take
\[
\theta_0=\pi-\frac{\pi}{2n}.
\]
Then \(\cos n\theta_0=0\) and \(\cos\theta_0=-\cos\frac{\pi}{2n}\). Nonnegativity gives
\[
0\le P(\theta_0)=1-2a\cos\frac{\pi}{2n},
\]
so
\[
a\le \frac{1}{2\cos\frac{\pi}{2n}}.
\]

This bound is attained by
\[
a=\frac{1}{2\cos\frac{\pi}{2n}},\qquad
b=\frac{(-1)^n}{2n}\tan\frac{\pi}{2n}.
\]
Indeed, writing \(\delta=\frac{\pi}{2n}\), the polynomial becomes
\[
P(\theta)=1+\frac{\cos\theta}{\cos\delta}
+\frac{(-1)^n}{n}\tan\delta\,\cos n\theta,
\]
and one checks by the standard inequality
\[
\cos\delta-\cos s+\frac{\sin\delta}{n}\cos ns\ge0
\qquad(0\le s\le\pi)
\]
with \(s=\pi-\theta\), that \(P(\theta)\ge0\) for all real \(\theta\).

Finally, at equality \(P(\pm\theta_0)=0\), forcing the rotated \(\beta\) to be real; differentiating at \(\theta_0\) gives
\[
b=\frac{(-1)^n}{2n}\tan\frac{\pi}{2n}.
\]
Undoing the rotation yields
\[
\boxed{\beta=\frac{(-1)^n}{2n}\tan\frac{\pi}{2n}\left(\frac{\alpha}{|\alpha|}\right)^n }.
\]
